author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: Episode substrate: a portable episode specification plus an SDK control surface that composes recipe, snapshot, bounded observation and computed verdict into one reproducible unit of work

pm-nfrhf0 names four things an agent training or evaluation loop needs and states plainly that pm nearly has all four and that what is missing is the composition. Each of the four now has an owner: pm-dkrmzv owns the workspace snapshot boundary, pm-rbcvt2 owns deterministic construction from a declared recipe, pm-e96opw owns computed per-criterion verdicts, and the bounded task projection is served by the existing read surface with pm-cxr0jb narrowing it to a declared intent. Nothing owns the composition itself, and the composition is the part an environment author would otherwise write from scratch every time.

The missing artifact is an episode: a named, bounded, reproducible unit of work with a declared beginning, a declared observation, a declared success condition, and a recorded end. Concretely it is two things.

First, a portable episode specification. A declared artifact that names the workspace recipe to construct from, the item or item set that forms the task, which fields the agent may observe and which are withheld for grading, the token budget the observation must fit, the criteria whose verdicts decide the outcome, and the limits -- wall clock, mutation count, tool budget -- that bound the run. This is distinct from pm-rbcvt2's recipe, which declares how a workspace is constructed and stops there. The specification declares what is asked of the agent and how the answer is judged, and it must be storable, shareable and re-executable by a different machine and a different pm build, exactly as a recipe is.

Second, an episode control surface in the public SDK. Open an episode from a specification and obtain an isolated instance. Read the current observation as a bounded projection. Let the agent act through the ordinary pm surface with no episode-specific API, because an environment that requires special calls is not measuring the tool anyone actually uses. Score the episode by evaluating the declared criteria against recorded state. Close it and obtain a result. The whole cycle must be reachable through the SDK alone, per pm-nfrhf0's own criterion that an environment can embed pm without shelling out.

Three properties matter more than the surface shape.

The grader must read only recorded state. If scoring consults anything the history does not contain, the result is not reproducible and the episode is not a verifier. This is what makes pm a substrate rather than scaffolding: reward is a function of the immutable record.

The agent must not be able to reach the grading fields. Withholding is a projection concern and belongs in the observation contract, not in an honour system. An episode where the success condition is readable is an episode that measures nothing.

The same loop must serve four workloads without special paths, because they differ only in what varies. A benchmark fixes the specification and varies the agent. An evaluation fixes the agent and varies the specification. Training varies both and consumes many episodes. A simulation-to-reality transfer varies the workspace scale between a synthetic instance and a real one, which is exactly the recipe-versus-real-workspace axis pm-rbcvt2 already draws. If the surface needs a different shape for any of the four, it is the wrong surface.

Scale boundaries are the same ones the rest of the project holds itself to. A single item and a single episode must work with no special path, and concurrent episodes must not share mutable state, so a fleet can run thousands at once against isolated instances.

This item owns the composition and the specification format. It does not own snapshots, determinism, criterion verdicts, or observation projection, all of which are declared dependencies with existing owners. It does not own the dataset produced by running episodes, which is its own item.

An episode specification is a declared, storable, shareable artifact naming the workspace recipe, the task item set, the observable and withheld field sets, the observation token budget, the grading criteria, and the run limits; A different machine and a different pm build within the supported format window can re-execute the same specification and obtain the same result; The public SDK opens an episode, exposes the bounded observation, scores it, and closes it with a recorded result, with no shelling out required; The agent acts through the ordinary pm surface only, with no episode-specific mutation API; Scoring reads recorded workspace state exclusively, and a negative control proves an episode fails to score when a grader consults state the history does not contain; Withheld grading fields are unreachable through every read surface available to the agent, proven by a test that attempts to read them from inside an episode; One benchmark, one evaluation, one training and one scale-transfer configuration all run on the same loop with no special path; A single item and a single episode work with no special path, and concurrent episodes share no mutable state; A worked exemplar in the repository runs a passing episode, a failing episode, and an episode that fails for the wrong reason

message: Filed to own the composition pm-nfrhf0 explicitly names as missing. Duplicate check: searched episode/step/reset/observation/trajectory, gym/environment/adapter, verifier/reward/predicate, and training/benchmark/eval; pm-nfrhf0 had zero descendants at filing time. The four component pieces are owned (pm-dkrmzv snapshots, pm-rbcvt2 determinism, pm-e96opw verdicts, pm-cxr0jb projections) and are declared as blockers or related rather than restated here.
